N is the segment count, Δ is segment length, λ is wavelength and a is wire radius. The shortest wavelength sets the maximum step. Changing the mesh may change the calculated impedance even when gain changes little.
DK7ZB, 145 MHz. Driven element 1010 mm, director 920 mm, spacing 210 mm, diameter 10 mm. Ideal conductors, centred source and free space. SWR reference: 50 Ω.
R / X (Ω), gain (dBi), F/B (dB), and average gain (AGT). The 5- and 81-segment rows are reference cases outside AntCalc’s automatic mesh.

The table shows a reference calculation for the two-element DK7ZB Yagi at 145 MHz with 21 segments per element. The example uses fixed parameters. Both real-ground methods use εᵣ = 13 and σ = 0.005 S/m.
